# Accessibility

Netherstone should work for everyone who wants to use it, with a mouse, a
keyboard or assistive technology. If something gets in your way, we treat
it as a bug.

## What you can adjust

In Settings › Appearance:

- **Theme:** Light, Dark or Match system, plus the darker Tyrant, Bloodline
  and Citadel themes.
- **Shard font:** Newsreader, Geist or your system font.
- **Text size:** Small, Default or Large.
- **Line width:** Narrow, Default, Wide or Full.

Common formatting in the editor has keyboard shortcuts, and controls show a
visible outline when you reach them with the keyboard.

## Supported environments

Netherstone runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. Its interface is shown by the
system's own web view (WebView2 on Windows, WebKit on macOS and WebKitGTK on
Linux), so how well screen readers and other assistive technology work
depends partly on the platform.

## Known limitations

- Netherstone has not yet been fully tested with screen readers. Labels and
  keyboard focus are in place, but there are likely gaps.
- Drawings are made with Excalidraw, which is hard to use without a mouse or
  pen and gives screen readers little to read.
- Only the onboarding screens follow your system's reduce motion setting so
  far.
- Exported PDFs, Word documents and web pages have not been checked with
  assistive technology.

## Reporting a barrier

Open a [Bug report](https://github.com/Netherstone-HQ/Netherstone/issues/new/choose)
and say what you were trying to do, what got in the way, and which assistive
technology you use, if any. If you would rather not post publicly, email
contact@netherstone.app.
